introduction: Registering a Will in Andhra Pradesh is a straightforward process that safeguards your assets and prevents future legal disputes. While registration is optional under Indian law, it is highly recommended to prove the authenticity of the document.
quickFacts:
Important to Know
  • Mandatory: No (Optional but recommended).
  • Stamp Duty: ₹0 (No stamp duty is required for a Will).
  • Registration Fee: Nominal (approx. ₹100 - ₹500 + User Charges).
  • Where to Register: Sub-Registrar Office (SRO) nearest to the Testator's (person making the Will) residence. Unlike property sales, you do not need to go to where the property is located.
  • Validity: A registered Will can be changed/revoked any number of times during your lifetime.
documentsRequired:
Documents Required

Note: You must carry the original and one set of photocopies of the following documents.
The Will & Testator Details
  • The Will Deed: Drafted on plain paper or good quality ledger paper (green paper). It does not need to be on Stamp Paper.
  • Testator's ID Proof: Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, or Passport.
  • Testator's Photos: 2 Passport-size photographs.
  • Medical Certificate (Recommended): A mental fitness certificate from an MBBS/MD doctor is highly advised if the testator is elderly (above 65) or ill. This prevents future claims that the person was not of "sound mind."
Witnesses Checklist
  • Two Witnesses: They must accompany you to the SRO.
  • Witnesses ID Proofs: ID proofs of both witnesses (Aadhaar/PAN).
  • Witnesses Photos: 2 Passport-size photos of each witness.
onlineApplication:
Online Application Steps

Andhra Pradesh uses the IGRS (Registration & Stamps Department) portal for slot booking. While the signing happens offline, you must book the appointment online.

  1. Visit the Portal: Go to the official IGRS AP website.
  2. Public Data Entry / Slot Booking: Look for the "Slot Booking" or "Public Data Entry" section on the homepage. You may need to create a simple login using your Mobile Number and OTP.
  3. Enter Details: Select "Document Registration". For "Nature of Document," select "Will" (or "Will Deed"). Enter the Testator’s details (Name, Father’s Name, Age, Address) and the details of the 2 Witnesses.
  4. Select SRO: Choose the Sub-Registrar Office (SRO) that covers your residential area.
  5. Book Appointment: Choose a convenient date and time slot.
  6. Acknowledgement: Download and print the Slot Booking Slip or Appointment Acknowledgement.
offlineApplication:
Offline Application (The Office Visit)

  1. Arrive Early: Reach the Sub-Registrar Office at least 15 minutes before your slot with all original documents and witnesses.
  2. Verification: Present your Appointment Slip and the Will to the counter officer. They will verify the ID proofs of the Testator and Witnesses.
  3. Biometrics: The Testator will be asked to sign the Will in the presence of the Registrar. Thumb impressions (fingerprints) and digital photos of the Testator and both Witnesses will be captured electronically.
  4. Witness Signing: The two witnesses will sign the Will and the registry book to confirm they saw you sign the document.
  5. Payment: Pay the nominal registration and user charges (usually cash or challan at the counter).
Special Case (Home Visit): If the person making the Will is bedridden or hospitalized and cannot move, you can apply for a Private Attendance. By paying an extra fee, the Registrar will visit your home or hospital to complete the registration.
afterApplying:
After Registration & Custody

Scanning & Return

The Sub-Registrar will scan the original Will. The original registered Will is returned to you immediately or within a few hours. The Registrar keeps the scanned copy in Book 3 (the register specifically for Wills).

Secrecy

Unlike property deeds, Wills are not open to the public for search. No one can apply for a copy of your Will while you are alive.

Safe Custody

You can choose to deposit the Will in a sealed cover with the Registrar for safekeeping (optional "Deposit of Will" service), or simply take the registered document home and keep it safe.

Pro-Tip

Always ensure the witnesses are younger than you and trustworthy, as they may be called upon to testify to the validity of the Will after your demise.
